THE BASS RIFF. Bass and strings, no drums, no voice: the one fixture that can point becomes the soloist. Clean white beam, no prism, snapping to a new wall on every downbeat -- four bars, four places -- and drifting across each bar with the bass. The row stays a dim blue field underneath so the beam cuts. Now: it NODS hard and FLASHES on beats 2 and 2-and-a-half, where the riff punches, from the very first bar -- and each turn to a new wall begins a beat early so the head arrives on the downbeat instead of leaving on it.

33.75s: bass and strings arrive together out of a one-second black. ONE beat of the whole row in white -- the row's single big statement in this phrase -- and then it drops to the blue bed and the head takes over. This was the biggest arrival in the first half of the song and it had been getting a dim bed fading in.

Bar 15: the red spark leaves on beat 2 and ARRIVES on the 'and' of 2 -- which is where this riff actually punches, every bar. A run is read when it lands, not when it starts, so it is aimed to land on the hit and takes a quarter of a second, not a whole beat. Left to right.

Bar 22, the C-major lift before the drop: the row at FULL in violet -- as far toward red as the build ever gets -- for two beats. Held at 0.85, not full: the last bar of the build was the brightest two seconds in the whole show, and the drop has to be bigger than the thing that led into it.
Then NOTHING for two beats, head included. Eight bars of the room warming and moving, and it stops dead. This silence is what makes the next beat enormous.
49.75s, THE DROP. Every lamp to full WHITE for one beat, snapped, no fade. The room has been blue for fifty seconds; this is the first white and the drums arriving.

The head goes RED with the PRISM for the first time all night: one red beam becomes six red rays, snapping wall to wall on every beat over a row that is now red and blue. The prism was withheld for fifty seconds so that this reads as an arrival. The prism PULSES on the front of every beat rather than sitting on, the tilt kicks on every beat, and each turn leaves a beat early so it lands on the beat.
52.76s: the whole band at full strength, six families at once. One full BEAT of white across the row, held, not an 80ms flash -- the head keeps snapping red underneath it.

Bar 26: a COLOUR WAVE. The row stays at full the whole bar; what travels is a white position across red, twice. Nothing gets brighter or darker, only the hue moves -- a look four cheap pars are not supposed to be able to do. Once, so it stays a surprise.

A genuine 200ms hole at 64.2s: the band falls to under half its own level right here, just before the drums come back full. Black for exactly as long as the hole, so the room breathes with the track instead of over it.
One beat of nothing before the drums come back full at bar 31.
Bar 31 lands. The build was kept cold on purpose so this is the first white the room sees.

Second drop: the head snaps side to side in red with the prism again, and now strobes on the downbeats too -- the thing it did not do at the first drop, so this one is recognisably the same move escalated.

Bar 38 dips to 50% between bars at 86% and gets no state - a second hole. Rather than fill it, put white flickers in it that accelerate into a hardware-strobe burst on the last beat, and let bar 39 arrive out of that. Anticipation is dark between pops, so the hole survives.

Third drop: the head's move a third time, escalated once more -- red, prism, and now strobing on EVERY beat, not just the downbeat. Same figure each drop, bigger each time, so the room learns it and then feels it grow.

The wave carries straight through the drop rather than stopping at it. The build ends with one lamp lit against three dark ones, which is a huge picture; if the drop settles into an even bed it reads as smaller than the run-up that led to it. So the row keeps crossing, a lamp per quarter beat, off a small floor. per_beat is crossings per beat now, so one means the light crosses the whole row once in the beat -- and it means the same thing on four lamps or sixteen.

THE LOUDEST KICK IN THE SONG at 102.76s -- full strength in the kick lane, the top of four consecutive bars that hold the four hardest hits on the record. Whole rig, full white, held for three beats. This is the peak of the show and it is placed on the hit rather than on a bar line. Four beats: this is the loudest kick in the song and the show's brightest moment lives here, not in the build.
